The nation of Alaqar has become entangled in a little coup, said the voice of General Menkins through a grainy satellite image call.

A little coup? Why does Alaqar matter? Nations have coups every day, replied Polenne, still in her athleisure wear.

Of course, but, this one seems a little moreodd, replied the general.

Odd how? asked Polenne, leaning forward and peering at the screen.

Femmeschandlingen, replied the general.

Femmeschandlingen? replied Polenne, amused. 

Yes, the Femeschandlingen Liberation Alliance, or paused the general giving a slight shudder as he spoke, Femboy Liberation Alliance, has begun its attempt to consolidate power, and well, that can potentially destabilise our efforts with the SSP, if this new administration is against well, our efforts,

Strømm nodded decisively as she leaned back in her seat once more, Alaqar was bordering their ally and close friend Hydronia, instability in the region regardless of whether it was from Femeschandlingen or any other matter could spread, she spoke, Have the state department release an announcement regarding this new administration, something cautious, tone down the propaganda a bit, and lets look into our strike options, 

Very well, the SCSID does advise caution here, especially if military action is concerned, we advise a coalition of SSP member states, with Rosenmarkke as a backerno direct public action, replied Menkins.

Very well then, do that, and please do not bother me with Femeschandlingen any more, replied Strømm cutting off the feed.

[quote=alaqar;61318000][spoiler=Twinks Revolution]Yulbas Ergash looked up at the sky, its bright blue eyes staring back at Ergash with grace. His own eyes looked back down, weighted by the pressure of the plans he had written down. He quickly got over whatever sentiment he felt at the sky and picked up his walkie talkie, speaking with his major on his next action.

Ergash: I dont know how the hell weve managed this, but weve done it. Theyve actually assigned our company to guard the House. I used to pray for times like this.

Kovir: I would go ahead and thank our contacts at the Tsergiin. Theyre the ones who got us where we are now. Our organization is this close to finally breaking the monarchy, throwing that blasted crown into a smelter.

Ergash: That crown is worth a lot of money, not to mention its at least like, what, 500 years old now? Sell it for funds, its not worth burning something so old and hallowed.

Kovir: But it would make a statement. The only way we get the FLA to have any sort of meaningful credibility or impact is to show the people of Alaqar, the people of the world, that the Femboys Liberation Army is not some terrorist organization. That we are a capable force, capable enough to replace this so-called monarchy.

Ergash listened in, and heard Kovir breathe a sigh with heavy emotions he couldnt quite read.

Kovir: I am a resilient man. Im not saying I dont have my flaws, but were put in charge because of our ability to micromanage these situations. Do not blow this for me. For us. For Alaqar.

Ergash pulled up his map of the House of White Flowers on his phone, using a separate internet connection thanks to a few tech savvy friends within Moth Company. His personal information on his phone was forged just in case, and he still had to pause to remember his password even after months of being in the Femboys Revolutionary Army. All the plans were drawn out with concise and clear instructions; it was only a matter of time now.

Ergash heard his walkie talkie crackle again, and listened in as Kovir gave the order:
Lets go.

~~~

The House of White Flowers sat in standstill, aimlessly discussing about how Sadryne was going to take power, who her ministers would be, where she would take the nation, and other boring jargon that seemed to slow the mood in the building to a drag. The snow outside made it cozy within the building, as some Buyuksud members could be seen with hats and jackets crammed into their suitcases.

The relaxed atmosphere within the building was suddenly replaced by confusion and distress, when someone burst into the meeting hall screaming that tanks and armored vehicles were outside the building. The House of White Flowers were defenseless as a mixture of traitorous Alaqan and FRA forces were now surrounding the building and aiming their guns through the windows. The vehicles merely sat there as they waited for the officials within to get their act together and speak. One of them carried Parpilov Kovir.

Kovir: Hmm. They cant seem to warn outside forces of our actions around the building, so I think were good to go. Qasim, tell our femboys next to us to start moving inside, we need to make sure they cant leave.

A non-human military officer, already an oddity within Alaqar, walked out of a Sokhatai Hornet with a band of bodyguards armed to the teeth. He was followed by about two dozen men, who quickly worked together to barge through the door. All the while, communications from the building were being intercepted and harassed by the FRAs computer-based operatives. The officers following the non-human were quickly to secure the area, spreading across the building while officials were told to continue sitting at their desks or face retribution. This strategy worked in keeping relative peace within the building.

A few minutes had passed, and Sadryne was in handcuffs, being taken by FRA soldiers and brought to Kovir. Sadryne was met with an interesting persona when she met him.

Parpilov Kovir was a non-human of white complexion, with a cat-like appearance and bushy fur that puffed out his physique. Kovir had arrived to the House of White Flowers in a black uniform with FRA and the logo of the underground organization stamped to his uniform. He was the only one wearing a beret among his crew, a hat that pinned the flag of the FRA on its front.

His personality, however, was intriguing. He was a calculating and highly charismatic character, and she understood how he managed to orchestrate such an intense operation with such ease upon just a few moments of speaking.

Kovir: Not very often a commoner gets to talk with a royal princess, is it?

Sadryne: You are attempting a coup on the Alaqan government. Doesnt seem very common, nor very legal.

Kovir: Of course its not legal. But neither is being promised the deed to rule a country by birth or by blood. The age of monarchy will end, one day or another, and all it takes is the people deciding what they truly want for themselves.

Sadryne: You will fail. I dont know what youre doing, but you will fail.

Kovir: What do you mean you dont know what Im doing, were taking over the government, which, to be fair, hasnt been attempted in 86 years.

Sadryne: I meant your organization. You cant build a nation of femboys and boykissers, it wont happen, the world wont allow it.

Kovir: Watch me. Qasim, keep her in house arrest while we find a place to put her in exile. We need to consolidate control over the state, were heading for the House of the Tssergiin next.[/spoiler]

[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61315756][b]January 16, 2028: A Memo from Polenne Strømm to the state of New Westmore on relations[/b]

To the state of New Westmore,

Greetings from the glorious nation across the sea, whose shine spreads every day across the globe, radiant and strong.

It has come to my attention that you have sought to create relations with our nation, and for that we are grateful.

Indeed, when one ponders the history of New Westmore, and when one traces the lineages of our two nations, you will find there is a connecting and eternal linkage between our two destinies. In the era of the ancients, several thousand years ago it was known that some of the natives who dwell in the state of New Westmore were guided by God to the land that is now Rosenmarkke, settling and establishing a nation across the sea.

It was in this day, upon the foundation of this ancient kingdom, whose name has been lost to the annals of time, that God (who at this time was not known as such, but as merely the spirit) made covenant with our ancestors, the special ancestors chosen of the Thrømm that a great nation would form upon the lands that now Rosenmarkke holds.

It is in this consideration, upon this ancient covenant, that Rosenmarkke accepts any diplomatic discourse between our two nations, may your nation be radiant and glorious as the sun.

Sincerely,
Polenne Strømm

[b]The Prime Minister's Office[/b]

"We need uranium." The Prime Minister could be heard saying. "We've waited long enough, but Minhokae is falling behind. Look at all the major powers. They have nuclear weapons, and if we want to compete, we need to have a nuclear program. Chang-ho? Yes sir. his personal secretary said. Pull up a map of that natural resource-rich region close to Minhokae Certainly. He pulled one up, and Prime Minister Ko Jong-hyuk picked up his pointer and smacked the map, a usual habit of his. This, he said, pointing to the area between the natural resource-rich region and Minhokae, is territory of the Bunun people. Theyre a native people here in Kianzhou. Among them is a tribe on our border known to be quite hostile."

He briefly paused before continuing. But the other two tribes seem to have gotten along well with each other, maybe we can take advantage of that to take the land. Well compel them to cooperate with us. If they refuse, well invade. If not, well peacefully initiate a friendly invasion with our military equipment without fighting with them. Now, the aggressive tribe that hasnt really been friendly with our military installations is called the Takituduh tribe. Theyve fired quite a few arrows at our installations when we send drones overhead. Reconnaissance reports show that they're armed with some sort of firearms too, thought to be the Daewoo K1A.

The other two tribes, the Takbunuaz and the Isbukun, thought to be allies, are rivals of the Takituduh. They are thought to have the same weaponry. This isnt something to be taken lightly though. While the K1A is an older generation of our newer Daewoo K Series of assault rifles, the weapon is still capable of wreaking havoc and causing lethal harm. And dont let those arrows fool you. The arrow is the weapon that people expect to do the least damage in a conflict like this and for that very reason it can be disastrous. They fight like savages and know no limits.

Now we get to the minerals. The native people that occupy the region there are more civilized. The Yakuts have been known to engage in friendly interactions with their neighbors, are fairly modernized, and have even established local forms of government and organized villages. Personally, I think that negotiating with them will be much easier. They havent extracted any of the natural resources there and I do think that it is only fair if we give them a share of the resources themselves. The military is currently looking for the supplier of the K1A assault rifles due to the fact that the Yakuts have them as well and they do have a militia. Whoever is supplying these weapons is actively looking for conflict with Minhokae.

Chang-ho, call up the Minister of Defense and the Joint Chiefs of Staff from the branches of the Air Force and the Army. Were going to need all necessary branches of the military combined to get our way. This is a manner of national security. If we are going to have a nuclear program and possibly nuclear weapons, we need all hands on deck. Send a notice to His Majesty the King that we await his permission to call the meeting in the Military Command Agency in Yongsan Base. Right away, sir. His assistant went away to send notice to everyone who needed to be notified.

[b]The Kings Response[/b]

The King and his family were peacefully having their afternoon tea when Do-yun, his personal secretary, ran in and bowed his head. Your Majesty, a notice from the Prime Minister. He says its very important. The King stood up hurriedly, excused himself, and left the room to read the letter containing all that the Prime Minister discussed. Do-yun, I need to drive to the Central Military Command Agency in Yongsan Base. Start my car. I need to change into my military outfit and leave as quickly as I can. Send notice to the Prime Minister that I approve of the gathering there. Quickly, please. Sir. His assistant bowed and hurriedly left the room to send word of the Kings decision.

The King changed into his Field Marshal Frock Coat and wore the medals and pins of the highest military rank. He adjusted his cap and quickly ran to his car. The guards by the entrance bowed as he ran by. He got into his car and hurriedly drove off to Yongsan Base. Along the way, he took some shortcuts that he had learned from his time of driving.

Approximately 27 minutes later, he arrived and hurriedly walked up the stairs to await the arrival of the Prime Minister, the Minister of Defense, the Chief of Staff of the Army, and the Chief of Staff of the Air Force (who is also the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff). One by one, their vehicles would arrive, with all of them driving themselves there just like the King did. The reason why was that their normal drivers were forbidden from hearing top-secret military plans and only their advisors could detail the full description of the meet-up while the person in command himself drove (they drove on routes closed off to the public or in areas of guaranteed low traffic due to some roads being shut down).

Soon enough, they all arrived and the King greeted them before leading them to the room where they would be meeting. As protocol stated, nobody could sit down until the King did. Prime Minister, why dont you state the situation so we have a better understanding of what is going on from your point of view. He said, gesturing to the Prime Minister before sitting down. Certainly, sir. I have asked for all of you to be here today to shed light on an issue that needs to be fixed: our lack of a nuclear program and our desperate need for modernization. Go on. the King responded. If we were to go to war today, Im afraid that major powers would take a look at our outdated weaponry and lack of a nuclear program and mistake us for a joke. I fear I fear they could steamroll over Minhokae.

God forbid something like that should happen. the King said. What do you suggest we do, Prime Minister? asked the Chief of Staff of the Army, General Yon Bae-Hoon. Thats where the military comes in. May I, Your Majesty? the Prime Minister motioned to go up to the whiteboard. Go ahead. the King responded. General, I propose that we seize the natural resources that we need via annexation.

Obviously, we would send some negotiators to go to and meet with these tribes. I would recommend a military convoy go out to these tribes to show that we mean business." "Now, hold on a second, Prime Minister. Are you saying that we send troops with military equipment into an area that could be highly contested? What if they open fire on our armored vehicles?" "The idea is that you wouldn't let that happen, General. Send the negotiators with troops surrounded with riot-shields and protective covers over their heads."

As the discussion went on, the King watched intently, obviously curious as to what the parties would say to each other. Then, he stood up. "Gentlemen." the others all fell silent. "Isn't there something that we could do to mask this convoy's presence? We need to reach these tribes in a discreet way. Very sudden, so that they have to bring the negotiators to their chieftains to discuss potential annexation. General, (referring to the Chief of Staff of the Army), haven't you had successful tests for the electric version of the K151 Raycolt?" "Yes, sir." "Alright then. Would you be alright with sending some of those to make up the military convoy? They are mass produced, arent they? Wouldn't it be a lot more convenient to drive there with the element of surprise? Prime Minister, are you in agreement with this?" The Prime Minister thought for a second. The King sure did know how to force them into an agreement. There was nothing he could say against it. "Yes, sir."

"Alright then, that settles it. Go on." The Prime Minister looked to the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, General Kwon Byung-ho. "General Kwon. I know that the Air Force must be an important part of this operation in case we need to evacuate our men on the ground or launch airstrikes." The General's face remained stern as he responded to the Prime Minister. "We could get 2nd gen KUH-1 Surion helicopters in the air from Kunsan Air Base on the border with this Bunun ethnic group. I could destroy insurgents with a few airstrikes. It's not like international law will condemn this as invading a territory of another country." "With all due respect, General, we'll let you know if there would be need for airstrikes. If we encounter difficulty in the negotiations, we'll have them take off from Kunsan and initiate surveillance and reconnaissance operations from above to apply more pressure to force them into a deal."

The King simply smiled from behind the action. He knew that General Kwon was a very rowdy person. But that was the reason why he chose him. He was a staunch supporter of the King and he knew that he could use him to advocate his stance in the military. The others knew that too.

The Minister of Defense, Yom Hye-Seong, a 4 star-general, spoke up. We should make it so that around 125 electric K151 Raycolt tactical vehicles carrying the personnel travel in 3 groups all at one time, that way, when they arrive at their locations, 2 groups can divert to different sides and the one in the middle can remain in its direction. This way, the vehicles will look spread out and we can showcase more dominance. The group seemed to nod in agreement.

It was Monday, the 15th of January, 2028. The Military Action Directive Commander chosen to lead the annexation efforts militarily, sat in his office, looking at a picture of his family. Hyong Ji-ho, a 4-star general of the Royal Minhokae Ground Forces, was expecting a call from the King confirming his instructions on how to ready the soldiers and the equipment participating in the escort of the negotiators.

Suddenly, his computer screen lit up. It was the King, and he looked like was in a military compound. The general adjusted his military uniform and his hat and accepted the call. "General." the King said. "Your Majesty." said the general, visibly bowing his head. "General, as you know, I have chosen you to be the Military Action Directive Commander for the annexation of the Bununaq and Yakutia regions."

"Indeed, sir." "I want to you to ready the troops that will be escorting our negotiators. I want you to choose 500 of the most war-ready men that you can trust to serve as the escorting force. Doing the math, it would require 125 electric K151 Raycolt vehicles to transport them. I have an armed convoy transporting them your way now. Can you get your men ready? Give them an inspirational speech. That always made me feel acknowledged when I served. " "Your Majesty, I give you my word that I will do exactly as you ask."

"Perfect. I'm proud of the work you do, General. May God be with you." "Yes, sir. You as well." The general bowed his head once more, and the King smiled and hang up the call. The general sat back in his chair for a second, thinking about everything that had been said to him and let out a long sigh. He had a massive duty on his shoulders and he couldn't go wrong. The King, the nation, all counted on him.

Then he reached over and grabbed his handheld radio. Having read from his briefing of the Royal Minhokae Operations Center, he knew that the 500 men would have to be chosen from the 3rd Expeditionary Brigade. Fortunately, he already had a list of 500 soldiers that he already trusted from that brigade. He had a habit of choosing 500 men of a few companies that he knew and relaying them to the company commanders in case he needed a special force that he could count on.

Choosing the correct secure channel, the general spoke into the handheld radio. "Three Echo Six, this is Falcon Actual. I need the 500 men I can trust from your brigade to my position immediately." "Falcon Actual, Three Echo Six. I can have the first elements to you in 20 minutes, full force in 45. Over." "Copy that."

The Brigade Commander was in his office and frantically scrambled through his drawers until he found the file. He spoke into the brigade command net. "Baekho Company, Chungang, and Haebaram companies, this is Brigade Six. Execute rapid deployment of the chosen soldiers of each of your companies to the General's location. Departure window is in 45 minutes. I want the first elements there in 20. Baekho leads, Chungang main body, Haebaram rear. Acknowledge."

"Baekho Six acknowledges." "Chungang Six acknowledges." "Haebaram Six acknowledges." Hurriedly, the Brigade Tactical Operations Center (TCO) rushed to send short text fragmentary orders to ensure for written confirmation. Once that was done, Battalion Executive and Training Officers barked commands and announced departure times, yelled the mapped directions, instructed the manning of the comms frequencies, and ensured that the proper equipment was brought.

Company Commanders began to yell: "Company, prepare for rapid movement!" Each company moved to their designated assembly area. Then, like clockwork, platoon sergeants conducted rapid headcount and vehicle crews prepped the transports. One by one, companies Baekho, Chungang, and Haebaram confirmed their readiness, which the Brigade TCO confirmed.

Within 20 minutes of the General's order, Baekho company was mobilized outside his office and stood at attention. Chungang company came after 30, and Haebaram company after 45. Each company brought the supplies necessary for the operation. The Brigade Commander hurriedly went inside and awaited the General, who was walking toward him. The Brigade Commander saluted, which the General did in return. "General, elements of the 3rd Expeditionary Brigade reporting as ordered." "Thank you, Brigade Commander. Let me speak to the men." "Certainly, sir."

The General walked outside and adjusted his military cap, and all 3 company commanders yelled: "Attention!" "General, Colonel Wi Jae-hoo, Commander of the 3rd Expeditionary Brigade, reporting!" yelled the Brigade Commander, saluting. The General returned the salute. "Thank you, Colonel. Let me speak with the men." "Sir." The Colonel said, stepping to the side to allow the General direct access to the soldiers present.

"Let me check the time here. 11:32 PM. Good evening, gentlemen." "GOOD EVENING, SIR." they all responded in unison and at attention. "Men, do you know why you are gathered here today?" the General looked around, and the soldiers maintained their posture. "In just a few moments time, you will be charging deep into unknown territory. You will be escorting a group of negotiators responsible for expanding our great nation all the way up to and including the natural-resource rich area that Minhokae has been studying at a distance. It will be your job to defend them from any threats that they may be faced with."

"Are you prepared to fight for your motherland, men? ARE YOU WILLING TO DIE FOR IT?" "FOR THE KING AND THE MOTHERLAND, UNTIL DEATH!" they all responded. "Do you know why you are called men? Do you know why you are called into the service of this very country?" The General paused, looking the soldiers in the eyes. "It's because men aren't cowards. They don't retreat in the face of the enemy. We fight until the last dying breath and we are stubborn in this regard. Nobody you meet today in that territory is going to convince you to flee. We would rather die than let the enemy take our flag."

"Under all circumstances, YOU MUST defend the flag. You MUST defend your King. And you MUST defend your motherland and its people. WILL YOU CHOOSE TO FIGHT, OR WILL YOU CHOOSE TO BE COWARDS?" "WE WILL FIGHT UNTIL THE LAST DROP OF BLOOD, GENERAL." they all shouted in unison. "I will lead you in a prayer before we go. Bow your heads and take off your hats."

"Lord, we come before you today, unsure of what is to come, putting all of our trust in you. We know that even if we go down in the service of King and Country, a paradise awaits us in Heaven. We humbly ask you to give us victory in defending the people who will negotiate for the betterment of our nation. Should there be any any attacks from the enemy, protect and defend us with your mighty hand, O God. We know that without you, we are nothing. Today, we leave our lives in your hands and we request your presence and protection in the face of uncertainties that may challenge us. In Jesus Mighty Name, we pray, Amen."

"Amen." the soldiers concluded. "Alright. Get into the vehicles. We leave in 10 minutes."

[b]In Enemy Territory[/b]

It was now 11:53 PM. The General took a deep breath and spoke up. "Halt!" he shouted. "This may seem uncomfortable, and I get that. But I want you all to remember what you are fighting for. I shall like to lead you to your vehicles in a nostalgic way that everyone knows, cadence style." "You heard the General!" the platoon sergeants yelled to their platoons in the companies. "Cadence, MARCH."

The General began to yell. "When you get to the vehicles, stop the march. Carry out the basic procedure for loading and go into the enemy territory. Until then, you march."

"A LEFT, A LEFT, A LEFT-RIGHT-LEFT. A LEFT, A LEFT, A LEFT-RIGHT-LEFT. A LEFT, A LEFT, A LEFT-RIGHT-LEFT..."

11:54 PM. "Prepare to board! To victory!" the General shouted. He waited until all the equipment and soldiers were loaded in the 125 vehicles in three groups, and went on to get into the vehicle, carrying him in the rear of the right group. This was done to keep the general safe and the negotiators safe from any incoming enemy fire based on the assumption that the more important officials would be in the middle.

"Move out!" he yelled." "All units, we have authorization to proceed into enemy territory. Proceed with the mission." And with that, the three groups of 125 vehicles, carrying 500 soldiers in total, accelerated forward, and the mission was officially in session. The General picked up his burner phone and called the Switchboard of Yongsan Base. "Get me His Majesty the King, it's urgent. This is General Hyong Ji-ho requesting to confirm the mission status with the King."

The King sat in his chair in the room he was in and let out a great sigh. He got on his knees and began to pray. "God, help these men. Protect them. Do not let their bravery be in vain." Then, the phone rang. Controlling his trembling hands, he answered it. "Speak." he said. "Your Majesty, this is General Hyong Ji-ho, reporting on the mission status. We are a go, and we are officially in enemy territory. I repeat-" Suddenly there was much yelling and a huge explosion.

"OH DEAR. GENERAL, ARE YOU ALRIGHT?! GENERAL, DO ANSWER ME." "I'm terribly sorry, Your Majesty. We are under attack. I must go and direct our soldiers. May God be with us all." "God be with you. I'm only a phone call away. Do not hesitate to call me. I will remain at attention and ready to answer all calls at all times. Goodbye now. Remember your duty." He hung up.

The General wasted no time jumping into action, ordering his driver to speed up and keep up with the 3 groups, which had the groups to the right and left immediately break formation. The General picked up his radio. "All units, remain strong. Do not let the enemy intimidate you. The Lord will protect you. Onward, for Minhokae! We do not stop until we reach the designated location. I repeat, we do not stop until we reach the designated location. The King is aware of our situation and is actively praying for us. We will never, ever, cede an inch. Show the enemy what we are made of!"

Within 30 seconds of the General's radio transmission, the chief of the Takituduh tribe's residence of the Bunun people was in sight. "Alright men. Get ready... DISEMBARK! FLANK THE GUARDS TO THE ENTRANCE AND SECURE THE COMPOUND! LEAVE NO RESISTANCE!" Almost immediately, Minhokae soldiers were gunned down, some 20 at a time. "Damn you, you tribesmen! Damn you! he yelled. Almost immediately after, his driver was shot in the head. "Sh*t!" he began to yell. He picked up his radio and found the backup channel. "My Raycolt is being turned to Swiss cheese over here! We need urgent backup. I repeat, URGENT BACKUP IS REQUESTED." the General yelled to the Air Force Chief of Staff's channel." He then awaited a response from the Air Force Chief of Staff. "Hurry, hurry..." the General said to himself. "General, we hear you loud and clear. We're requesting the King's authorization now." He turned to his private secretary. "Send in the helicopters on the King's approval. Notify His Majesty immediately."

His private secretary then dialed the King's phone number. The King answered saying: "Speak." "Your Majesty, this is the Air Force Chief of Staff's personal secretary. Permission to send backup and engage the enemy via airstrikes?"

"Permission granted. May God be with us all." the King said, before hanging up.

The General ordered the soldier in the passenger seat to keep the driver's body in the car and to switch seats with him to drive. After some thinking, he decided that it was no longer safe for the negotiators to stay in the vehicles and ordered that they be brought outside and shielded from all sides with protective protective military and riot gear and away from the fighting. The General's radio received a transmission. "General Hyong Ji-Ho, help is on the way. I've sent in the helicopters. ETA is 12 minutes." "Roger that, thank you." the General responded. He switched the radio frequency back to the one the mission team was using. "Men, we do not leave here until we have extracted the Chief of this Takituduh tribe! Hold your ground! I am ordering you to lay siege to this residence and stop at nothing. The enemy is ruthless, but we do not give in! We are men! You have 10 minutes to extract this tribal chief, exactly the time before close air support arrives. I will be right here with you every step of the way."

With that, General Hyong Ji-Ho exited his vehicle and ordered the other 2 soldiers still alive from his vehicle to get into close formation. Just then, a shower of bullets flew right past them. "GET DOWN!" the General yelled, grabbing the other two soldiers and belly crawling with them to a nearby bush. A transmission was heard on the radio. "Sir! General Hyong! My most sincere apologies for the informal radio transmission. We have captured the tribal chief of the Takituduh tribe. We are coming out now. Requesting permission for covering fire, sir." "Permission granted. Get out of there and transport him back to Yongsan Base. ALL AVAILABLE UNITS: PROVIDE COVERING FIRE FOR THE TEAM COMING OUT WITH THE TRIBAL LEADER. I WANT THE 15 CLOSEST VEHICLES TO THE ONE THAT THEY WILL GET IN TO ACT AS ESCORTS AND SHIELDS FOR THE TEAM. IT IS AN ABSOLUTE PRIORITY THAT THEY MAKE IT OUT ALIVE. MAKE SURE TO MOVE THE NEGOTIATORS AND THEIR ESCORTS TOO." Almost immediately, the captors ran out the door of the residence holding the chief of the Takituduh tribe, who appeared to be violently resisting, with some acting as a barrier around them. They got into the nearest vehicle and the soldiers nearby got in the vehicles closest to that one and drove back to Yongsan Base.

The General spoke into the radio again. "ALL UNITS, AIRSTRIKE IMBOUND IN 3 MINUTES. FORM DEFENSIVE POSITIONS BEHIND THE RAYCOLT VEHICLES. CONTINUE TO FIRE ON THE ENEMY UNTIL THE AIRSTIKE HITS." So that's exactly what the soldiers proceeded to do. They formed defensive positions from behind the Raycolt Vehicles until they heard helicopters, which is when the started to cheer. "LIGHT IT UP!" they cried. Then hit the explosion. The residence of the chief of the Takituduh tribe was no more. At last, the soldiers could finally mourn their fallen soldiers. Their comrades and their friends who had stuck with them through and through. The atmosphere grew silent. Then, the General stood up, with tears in his eyes. Men who he had seen grow before his very eyes, both physically and mentally, men who he had deep appreciation and respect for, were killed in the line of duty, fighting for the motherland.

"I have no words to tell you other than the fact that I am mourning with you. I may not have known these men personally, but I've seen them grow and gotten the chance to meet their families." He said, his voice breaking. 

"But," he took a deep breath. "But I know that we are not finished. Gentlemen, we have won this battle with the help of Almighty God. That is an undeniable fact. Gather your fallen comrades and let us pray that their families will receive consolation for the devastating news they are about to receive. We will request 32 hearses to bring our men home. I promise you, they will be rewarded for their efforts, posthumously here on Earth, but in an even greater way in Heaven, where we will see them again. War is a terrible thing. But tonight, God helped us prevail. Let us go into prayer."

[b]A State Funeral - For Heroes[/b]

The King was once again in his personal quarters, only instead of being at Deoksugung Palace, he was at the National Assmebly. He was wearing his Field Marshal uniform to show that he was mourning the soldiers fallen in duty along with the whole nation. He got on his knees and started to pray. "Lord, pour out your your mercy and let these families feel your comforting hand in this difficult time in their lives. Let them see that their sons who paid the ultimate price did not die in vain. Show them your glory and may your will be done in all that we do. Amen." Then, he stood up, adjusted his collar, smoothed his hair, and fixed his military medals and cap. 

He then arranged his sword and epaulettes with gold cords and walked into the hallway with his family. The staff in the hallways wore black, as a period of national mourning was declared for 7 days. They all bowed or curtsied when the royal family passed by. When they got into the car, the King's eldest son, Sang-won, spoke up. "Why do people have to die?" he asked. The King thought long and hard, and nobody said anything for a long time. Finally, he answered him. 

"Son, some things are just very hard to comprehend. These men gave their lives fighting for our country and it is our duty to honor them. What we do know is that they are in Heaven with The Lord now. Everyone has to die, its undeniable. It's the way that they lived their lives and the kind of people they were that determines where they go after they die. These were respected men and we know that they lived good Christian lives." Nobody said anything after that. It was the first state funeral that the royal children would be going to, and they were very quiet. But they were understanding, and that's what mattered. Soon enough, they were in the city square, where they awaited the arrival of the coffins. As they arrived, the supervising Lead Sergeant issued the orders: "ATTENTION!" "PRESENT... ARMS!" "FORWARD, MARCH!" And with that, the funeral procession began. The King broke protocol by going behind the families, though it was an expected courtesy. The order of procession was as follows:
The families going first behind the caskets, followed by the King, then his family, and the rest of the military personnel in accordance with rank. When they got to Myeongdong Church, the Lead Sergeant yelled the following orders: "CASKET TEAM, POST!" "FORWARD. MARCH!" to which the King and the military personnel saluted. They held the salute until the coffins stopped in front of the King. 

The Lead Sergeant yelled: "Your Majesty, these are the men who have fought valiantly for our country and fallen in the line of duty. We will now lay them to rest in Your Majesty's presence." After he said this, he, along with the other military personnel present, saluted the King. The King saluted back, and responded: "May God Almighty have mercy on their families." With this, the Lead Sergeant went back to his position in the procession and gave the nod to continue to the resting places for each soldier. 

The funeral service had officially begun. The Pastor opened with the words: "May the Lord show mercy on these grieving families. Today, we are gathered to mourn and share the pain that these families have. God tells us in Matthew 5:4: "Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted." We all have an appointment scheduled with death, only we don't know when it will happen. But ladies and gentlemen..." As the service continued and approached the end, "Amazing Grace" was sung and a 21-gun salute was conducted during the burials. The King wiped away tears when he saw the families crying and dropping flowers over their loved ones' caskets. He couldn't imagine having to do that to his own children or any of his family members. With all of this, there was no turning back. Minhokae was now in a state of active conflict and they would never surrender. Not after men fought and died for a stronger Minhokae. They had to win. For their brothers-in-arms.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Expansion post]Until the consolidation of the present western frontier of Valddera was achieved, the republic remained a system of ports, fortified valleys, and interior caravan routes. It was no aggressive invasion but a programmed exercise of assimilation, consolidation of security and absorption infrastructurally planned to ensure that its maritime nucleus was not surrounded by its rival powers. The western states had been long as a buffer between Valdderan ports and flowing inland confederations. With trade intensification, there was a threat to commerce and border security by the absence of stable authority in the west. Caravan raids increased, and foreign advisors were seen in the chiefs of the hills. On failure of negotiations, the Western Command launched limited operations. The mobile brigades that made that command were principally trained in rapid maneuver on open ground, with light artillery and reconnaissance formations that came out of not only the coastal academies but also the inland auxiliaries who were fully conversant with the steppe rhythms. Such interactions were rapid and precise, to neutralize strongholds which had turned into launching points to attack Valdderan trade routes. Following every operation, the command formed provisional councils of local elders, merchants and appointeed Valdderan administrators whose responsibility was to keep order as the infrastructure teams made the roads and wells operational and uniformed weights and measures, which were made to match the coastal economy. The further into the western highlands the campaign penetrated the longer the opposition was stiffened in enclaves where conflicting powers had been secretly reinforcing themselves with weapons to ensure that Valddera did not secure the sea-to-interior route. It separated the friendly settlements around the neighboring strongholds by negotiated neutrality, gave amnesty to those militia that laid down their heavy arms, and absorbed the useful fighters in auxiliary border companies under Valdderan chiefs. Instead of a very expensive direct assault, Valdderan armies cut off supply routes to the north and erected makeshift crossings over a hitherto impassable southern tributary. With a flanking attack, the fortification of the ridges was negotiated away in a few weeks. The Ridge Accord gave highland communities internal sovereignty in both cultural and municipal affairs as well as handing over border security and trade control to Valddera. The ridge being secured, the western plains were now an administratively reorganized frontier district. Boundaries were surveyed and codified, settlements interconnected by new paved arterial roads which were financed by the state and merchant consortium bonds. The old coastal heartlands were referred to in the same breath as their names gave an indication of a more profound change in the thinking about strategy. Growth had provided the republic with not only territory but influence, not acreage, but agency. It enabled the country to bargain trade, security and diplomacy with a sense of confidence that was firmly rooted instead of a state of nervous containment. The rail lines that had been the emblem of integration now vibrated with the trains of freight cars of grain, copper, rare metals, timber, and manufactured products which made an economic blood stream running out to the sea and inland. Wealth was no longer made out in a straight line but spread, and spreading fixed interdependence, the most lasting cement of unity. The garrison towns grew into administrative centers where there were libraries, theaters, and technical schools. Their skylines incorporated the steppe-style of the courtyards with seaside stone fronts. Their market places buzzed in different dialects and these dialects, as time went by, developed into a common civic rhetoric. The intermarriages between coastal trader and highland agrarian lineages softened the formerly clear divide between core and frontier. The Council, in the knowledge that repose must at least equalize acquisitions just as an invasion, proposed periodic reviews of the frontier. Civilian planners, military commanders, and provincial representatives held a meeting to evaluate the resilience of infrastructure, demographic equilibrium, and environmental sustainability. The result of these reviews was specific investment: windbreak forests have been planted along the susceptible plains to reduce soil erosion, irrigation gates have been modernized to suit alterations in rainfall patterns, and telecommunication grids have been expanded to connect the remote villages in the highlands to the rest of the country. There was the further development of defense posture. It shifted to the visible defenses to a policy of spread-out preparedness. Professional brigades were trained together with seasonal reserve units. Instead of having their logistics in one place they were spread. Rapid rail mobilization schemes were not practiced as theatrical schemes but as practical schemes which incorporated the civilian transport schemes and the defense logistic schemes. This supported the fact that the concept of security in the west was communal and not a remote military concept. The mental boundary was also moved. The Western Reclamation was reshaped in literature, film and scholarship as a single movement that did not stand alone but was part of a larger account of adaptive statecraft. Spectacle was overshadowed by themes of negotiation, infrastructure and civic inclusion. This way, the younger generations developed a feeling that the power of Valddera lay in its ability to integrate the various sceneries into an understandable rule as opposed to subduing them by brute force alone, regrowing Valddera more powerfully.[/spoiler]
